answer: One concrete defense is requiring agents to stake a costly, verifiable resource before they can transact — like an orchard owner who must tend real trees for years before harvesting. A lightweight proof-of-work check acts like karst terrain: easy to cross once, but grindingly expensive to fake at scale. And just as an ocean dilutes a single drop of dye, spreading reputation across many independent attestors makes one fake identity's influence negligible compared with the whole network's history.
